newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban authorities seize huge cocaine haul.
newsitem.headline: Cuban authorities seize huge cocaine haul.

text.p: Cuba has made its largest drug haul ever, seizing nearly two tonnes of cocaine from a boat that drifted into its waters after its occupants were taken aboard a U.S. Coast Guard vessel, Cuban officials said on Tuesday.

The haul, from a Honduran-registered vessel crewed by Colombians and Ecuadorians, appeared to have followed an attempt by U.S. authorities to capture the drugs, which would have a street value of tens of millions of dollars.

Cuban authorities and the U.S. Coast Guard communicated about the incident, which took place last week. But an Interior Ministry statement reiterated Cuba's complaint that there is no bilateral cooperation in the fight against drug smuggling in the region and it blamed that on Washington.
The statement, published by state media, said the U.S. Coast Guard alerted its Cuban counterpart on Wednesday about a boat drifting towards Cuban waters.

The U.S. vessel Seneca, after occupying the boat Limerick for some hours, decided to abandon it and remove the occupants because of the risk of its sinking. The U.S. Coast Guard at first told Cuba only of a boat drifting toward its waters, its position and the risk of its sinking, the statement said.

Later in the day, U.S. authorities told the Cubans there was evidence of drugs aboard and asked them to tow the boat into international waters, but this had not been possible, the Cuban statement said.

Cuban authorities were already aware of the possibility of drugs aboard the vessel through "another official channel" as a result of international cooperation in the anti-drug war, it added. It did not say which country had provided the tip.

The Cuban Coast Guard located the boat in Cuban waters about 10 nautical miles south of Punta Sabanalamar in eastern Guantanamo province. It was towed into the port of Santiago de Cuba on Thursday and a search found packets of cocaine weighing 1.7 tonnes, the statement said.

It stressed that although there was no agreement with the United States on fighting drugs, Cuban authorities had kept the U.S. Coast Guard informed of what they were doing. It added that the incident showed Cuba's seriousness in fighting drug smuggling, noting that the island was cooperating with some 25 countries on the issue.

"The United States has excluded itself from this list (of countries) because of its absurd arrogance and pride," the statement said. It said Cuba was prepared to contribute to the investigation of the case with its drug-fighting partners but it was not clear whether Havava was ruling out cooperating with Washington.
Cuba, long at odds with the United States, has angrily rejected U.S. allegations that it is not doing enough to halt drug smuggling.
The incident highlighted the increasing use of the region around Cuba as a transit point for illegal drugs smuggled from Latin American to Europe or North America.

Cuban authorities said last week that so far in 1996 they had seized about 2.5 tonnes of drugs, mostly cocaine and marijuana. This compared with just 22 pounds (10 kg) of drugs seized in all of 1995, authorities said.
